title: the Lalita Sahasranama (selections)
hook: the goddess has a jeweled city, and then the hymn gives her a second address: inside the body

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Lalita Sahasranama and its five acts: making, keeping, withdrawing, concealing, and grace. What turned up for you after being hidden? Day one thousand one hundred five.

Same goddess, two addresses. Early in the Lalita Sahasranama, she lives somewhere grand. The names place her in the middle of an ocean of nectar, in a forest of kadamba trees, in a house of wish-granting gems, seated on a throne. It reads like a palace you'd need a map to find. Then, further on, the hymn turns. It gives her a second address, and this one isn't far away at all. It's a human body, starting at the base of the spine. Today, the names that move the goddess indoors.
screen: `AN OCEAN OF NECTAR, A HOUSE OF GEMS.` → `THEN A SECOND ADDRESS.` → `INSIDE A HUMAN BODY.`

segments.voice: Here is the run, in paraphrase, and it moves like a climb. Her one dwelling is the muladhara, the root center at the base of the spine. She pierces the knot of Brahma. She rises within the manipura, the center at the navel. She pierces the knot of Vishnu. She stands within the ajna, the center between the brows. She pierces the knot of Rudra. She rises onto the thousand-petaled lotus at the crown of the head. And from there, she pours down streams of nectar. A few names on, the hymn calls her bright as a streak of lightning, dwelling above the six centers, and then names her outright: Kundalini, the coiled one, fine as the thread inside a lotus stalk. So the queen of the jeweled city is also a power curled at the root of a human body, rising, untying knots, and raining nectar back down. In Shakta Tantra and in the Sri Vidya tradition, these names are read as a map for inner practice, and those practices are taught by a teacher, in person, with care. This path doesn't teach them. Others hear the same names devotionally, as the hymn saying, in its own way, that the goddess isn't only out there. And some readers notice the three knots. Each one carries the name of a great god, Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, and the goddess passes through all three. What looked like a palace far away turns out to have a door much closer in.
screen: `FROM THE ROOT OF THE SPINE.` · `THROUGH THREE KNOTS.` · `TO THE LOTUS AT THE CROWN.` · `KUNDALINI, THE COILED ONE.` · then, large: `A DOOR MUCH CLOSER IN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: a gentle climb of attention, nothing more. Sit tall, without strain. First, feel where you meet the chair or the floor, the base of the spine, solid and supported. Stay a few breaths. Then let attention move to the belly, rising and falling. Then to the space between the brows. Then to the crown of the head. No pushing, no picturing energy. Just noticing, place by place, the way you'd walk slowly up a staircase in your own house. If you pray, you can greet the goddess at each step. If you don't, let the climb be quiet. The bell holds the time.
The Lalita Sahasranama. Today, the names that give the goddess a second home: rising from the root of the spine to the lotus at the crown. Today's word.
Your line: the Lalita Sahasranama, in selections. Today, once, while waiting somewhere, sit tall and take three breaths from the base of the spine to the crown. Day one thousand one hundred five.

howItsDone: In Shakta Tantra and the Sri Vidya tradition, the kundalini names of the Lalita Sahasranama are read as a map of inner practice taught by a guru; other devotees simply recite them as praise of the goddess within.

fork.setup: you've climbed with the names from the root of the spine to the lotus at the crown. what does the goddess do next, in the hymn?
fork.reveal: the name after the crown says she pours down streams of nectar: the climb ends in something given back.

original.note: Sanskrit kuṇḍalinī: 'the coiled one,' a name the hymn gives the goddess as the power at the root of the spine.

trapdoor: what you thought: kundalini is a workout or a yoga-class word.
what it means: in the Lalita Sahasranama, Kundalini is a name of the goddess herself, rising through the body to the crown.
what a scholar hears: mūlādhāraikanilayā, brahmagranthivibhedinī … sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā, sudhāsārābhivarṣiṇī: a run of names read in Sri Vidya as a map of inner practice.
